_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). THIS TILE IS TWO DIFFERENT PAINTINGS STACKED. Above y~0.62 it is pure distant summit: pale silk, long wandering 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre contours, and ridge crests loaded with 点苔 moss dotting -- there is not one animatable tree in the entire top 60% of this tile. Below y~0.62 the scroll drops into the middle distance and a whole settlement appears: a thatched pavilion at the lower left, a big autumn 夾葉 tree beside it, conifer stands, a great blue-green tree at centre-right, and pine groves marching along the slopes and cliff shoulders. EVERY leaf object in this file lives in that bottom band. THE DECOYS, in order of how badly they will fool a colour pass: (1) THE MOSS-DOTTED RIDGE CRESTS, x 0.0-0.74, y 0.05-0.51. At thumbnail size these dark bands read exactly like rows of distant treetops. Zoomed 4x they are accumulations of small dark dabs laid along the top edge of a rock slope -- no stem, no branch, no trunk anywhere in them. This is the surface that made the rock move last time. kind:rock, leavesVisible:false, no exceptions. (2) SUB-FLOOR REAL TREES INSIDE THAT SAME BAND. Around x 0.15-0.48, y 0.32-0.44 there genuinely ARE tiny distant conifers with a visible vertical stem and horizontal branch layers -- I checked at 4x and the wood is there. They are real trees and they are deliberately NOT catalogued: each one is roughly 0.03-0.045 of the tile on its short side, under the 0.06 floor, and any box big enough to hold a row of them would be more than half rock. Swaying them would read as jitter and would drag the ridge with them. Left as rock on purpose. (3) VERTICAL HEMP-FIBRE STREAKS ON THE CLIFFS, worst at x 0.78-1.0, y 0.20-0.90 and x 0.44-0.58, y 0.81-0.95, where long parallel strokes fan downhill and mimic a spray of pine needles. No wood, no leaf glyph. (4) BLUE-GREEN MOSS WASH ON STONE at x 0.80-0.87, y 0.86-0.97 -- the same blue-green pigment that colours the real foliage, applied here as dotting on a rock face. Colour alone cannot separate this from a canopy; only the presence of wood can. (5) THE TALL BARE SPIRES at x 0.20-0.29, y 0.555-0.66 are the opposite error: they ARE trees, with clear straight stems and small horizontal barbs, but they carry almost no leaf mass -- winter-bare 寒林 spires. Recorded as trunk, leavesVisible:false, so a leaf animator ignores them. Two things too small to catalogue but worth knowing about: a thin blue-green tree clipped by the LEFT EDGE at x 0.0-0.045, y 0.72-0.93, and a tiny pale-roofed outbuilding at x 0.63-0.66, y 0.847-0.861 tucked into the slope trees. The pavilion, the autumn tree and the blue-green tree are the three shapes worth real animation effort in this tile; everything else on the slopes is a search region over rock.

objects.name: moss-dotted ridge crest, upper left
objects.note: THE PRIMARY DECOY OF THIS TILE. A broad slope of pale silk whose top edge carries a dense band of 点苔 moss dabs, thickest x 0.0-0.35 at y 0.09-0.20 and running down-right to x 0.45 by y 0.30. Verified at 4x: dabs only, not one stem or branch. NEVER animate

objects.name: lower left flank of the same ridge
objects.note: the slope falling away below the crest; long wandering hemp-fibre contours with scattered dotting. Clipped by the left edge, continues into t008

objects.name: long ridge sweeping down-right across the centre
objects.note: SEARCH-REGION CAVEAT IN REVERSE -- this box is rock but it CONTAINS real sub-floor trees. The genuine little distant conifers described in decoy (2) of the tile note sit inside it around x 0.15-0.48, y 0.32-0.44. They are wood, and they are still labelled rock here because they are under the size floor and inseparable from the dotting around them. If a later per-pixel pass ever wants them, this is where to look -- but do not sway this box

objects.name: sharp dotted peak, right of centre
objects.note: a pointed summit whose crest at x 0.78-0.88, y 0.30-0.36 carries the same moss dotting plus a few tiny tree glyphs far under the floor. Rock

objects.name: pale cliff wall, upper centre
objects.note: almost empty silk with a few long single contour strokes describing a huge face; the emptiest passage in the tile. Clipped by the top edge

objects.name: dotted rock shoulder, upper right
objects.note: hemp-fibre strokes with heavy dotting along the lower lip of the shoulder. Clipped by the top and right edges

objects.name: cliff wall down the right edge
objects.note: long vertical hemp-fibre strokes running the full height; decoy (3). Continues into t010/t011

objects.name: empty mist band separating summit from settlement
objects.note: untouched silk, the atmospheric gap that makes the peaks read as distant. Nothing in it; listed so a mask pass does not go hunting here

objects.name: three tall bare tree spires behind the pavilion
objects.note: straight vertical stems with short horizontal barbs and only tiny tufts at the tips -- 寒林 winter-bare trees. Real wood, so not rock, but there is no leaf mass to move. leavesVisible:false is deliberate: a leaf animator must skip these or it will wave bare sticks

objects.name: dark fir stand left of the pavilion
objects.note: spiky layered needle sprays on visible thin vertical trunks -- structure confirmed at 3x. Bare silk shows between the trees, so the box is loose around the crowns but every dark mark inside it is needle, not stone

objects.name: dark fir stand behind and right of the pavilion
objects.note: taller and denser than the stand to its left; the tallest crown reaches y 0.645. The bare spires (bare-spires-tall) stand in front of the left half of this box and must be cut out of any mask built from it

objects.name: thatched pavilion at the lower left
objects.note: a wide combed thatch roof from y 0.79 to y 0.87, a row of thin posts below it, and a railed platform along y 0.93-0.97. Drawn in fine outline with a warm ochre wash on the thatch. RIGID

objects.name: crown of the red-orange autumn tree
objects.note: the signature shape of this tile: large 夾葉 double-outline lobed leaves, some filled with a red-orange wash, some left pale. Densest leaf mass anywhere in these three tiles and the best sway subject here. Ochre limbs thread through it and are wood

objects.name: lower leaf mass of the autumn tree
objects.note: the same tree below the main limb fork; leaves hang down behind the pavilion roof. Left edge reaches x 0.255 where an orange-washed spray overhangs the thatch. Below y 0.90 it is rock and the pavilion platform

objects.name: trunk of the autumn tree
objects.note: heavy pale-ochre column with dark contour on both sides, running from the limb fork at y 0.74 down to the rock at y 0.90. Narrow, but it is the wood that proves the two leaf boxes above are a tree. RIGID

objects.name: limb sweeping right out of the autumn tree
objects.note: a thick ochre bough curling right and down out of the fork, clearly visible in the gap between leaf clusters. A hinge should pivot leaves about this, not displace it

objects.name: dark ink pine cluster, centre
objects.note: a tight group of dark pines standing in front of a pale grey rock mound; crowns at y 0.64, trunks visible in the lower half. The mound behind them (rock-mound-behind-pines-centre) shows through the gaps, so this box carries some rock -- treat as a SEARCH REGION and mask on the dark ink

objects.name: crown of the great blue-green tree, centre right
objects.note: a broad drooping canopy of small blue-green leaf strokes hanging in curtains. The second-best sway subject in the tile: it stands clear against empty silk on its right and top, so the silhouette is clean

objects.name: lower leaf curtain of the blue-green tree
objects.note: the canopy sweeping down-left below the main limb; left edge reaches x 0.59. Its bottom edge at y 0.725 is where the leaves stop and the slope behind takes over

objects.name: ochre limb of the blue-green tree
objects.note: an unmistakable yellow-ochre bough sweeping left-down out of the crown, the clearest piece of exposed wood in the tile. This is what makes the two boxes above a tree rather than a wash. RIGID

objects.name: band of dark trees on the slope, upper left of the ravine
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. Real trees -- vertical trunks and flat layered canopies confirmed at 3x -- but they are strung along a rock slope and roughly a third of this box is stone. Mask per pixel on the dark ink before moving anything

objects.name: band of dark trees on the slope, right of the ravine
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, same caveat as slope-trees-upper-left. Trunks are legible under the canopies at y 0.78-0.84

objects.name: dark trees down the gully, lower centre
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. The densest of the three slope bands; a tiny pale-roofed outbuilding sits inside it at x 0.63-0.66, y 0.847-0.861 and is rigid architecture, too small to give its own entry

objects.name: pines on the cliff shoulder, right
objects.note: a row of pines with dark flat canopies over pale vertical trunks, growing out along the lip of the right cliff. Wood is unambiguous at 4x. The cliff face below and right of them is hemp-fibre rock (decoy 3) and must not be swept in

objects.name: pine grove on the ridge crest, bottom right
objects.note: the clearest wood in the whole tile: six or seven dark vertical trunks with spreading flat crowns standing along a ridge top. Nothing ambiguous here. Continues into t010

objects.name: dark pines along the bottom edge, centre
objects.note: spiky dark conifer crowns clipped by the bottom edge, standing in front of the pavilion platform. Continues below the tile into the next band

objects.name: pale grey mound behind the centre pines
objects.note: a smooth rounded hill in flat grey wash with a dotted crest; the dark pines stand in front of it. It is the rock contaminating dark-pines-centre

objects.name: hemp-fibre rock face under the autumn tree
objects.note: DECOY. Long fine parallel strokes fanning downhill directly below the autumn tree's right limb -- at a glance a hanging spray of needles, at 3x not one leaf glyph. Adjacent to real foliage on three sides, so this is the pair most likely to be mislabelled

objects.name: cliff face, lower right
objects.note: vertical hemp-fibre strokes with blue-green moss dotting on the stone at x 0.80-0.87, y 0.86-0.97 -- decoy (4), the same pigment as the real canopies. Colour cannot separate these; only wood can

objects.name: open rock slope along the bottom edge
objects.note: the ground the settlement stands on, drawn as pale contoured ledges with scattered dotting. Clipped by the bottom edge
